propositions.text: RPD received an application to reinstate under rule 53 on March 24, 2011.
propositions.quote: On March 24, 2011, the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) received an application to reinstate under rule 531 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD received an application to reinstate under rule 53 on March 24, 2011, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicant is a Colombian citizen who withdrew her refugee claim and wants to return to Colombia.
propositions.quote: This application concerns XXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of Colombia. It follows the notice, received by the RPD on December 30, 2010, to withdraw her refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Applicant changed address and requested quick response due to inability to stay long at new location.
propositions.quote: She stated that she was no longer living with her mother, step-father and half-brother at XXXXXX, but was instead living at XXXXXX, XXXXXX, XXXXXX. She also stated that she would appreciate a quick response because she could not stay at that location very long.

propositions.text: RPD sent notice confirming withdrawal to applicant's new address on January 5, 2011.
propositions.quote: A notice confirming the withdrawal of her refugee protection claim was sent to the applicant by the RPD on January 5, 2011, to the new address indicated by the applicant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicant is Colombian, withdrew her claim, changed address, requested quick response, and RPD confirmed withdrawal by notice.

propositions.text: Applicant faxed note on January 4, 2011, repeating desire to leave quickly due to no money and no family support.
propositions.quote: On January 4, 2011, she faxed a new note repeating that she wanted to leave the country as quickly as possible because she was no longer living with her family and she had no money.

propositions.text: Applicant booked flight from Toronto to XXXX on XXXX and passport was sent by father but seized by customs.
propositions.quote: She also stated that she had already booked a flight from Toronto to XXXX on XXXX. She stated that her father had sent her passport to her by UPS, from Colombia, on December 20, 2010, that her passport had arrived in the country on December 22, 2010, but that it had been seized by [translation] "customs".

propositions.text: Applicant was trying to get passport back to catch flight on XXXX, 2011.
propositions.quote: She was therefore trying to get her passport back in order to catch her flight on XXXX, 2011.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts applicant's January 4, 2011 fax about leaving quickly, flight booking, passport sent but seized, and efforts to retrieve it.

propositions.text: Panel reviewed application and affidavit; applicant withdrew claim after fight with mother who kicked her out.
propositions.quote: The panel reviewed the application presented by the applicant and the affidavit accompanying it. The applicant indicated that she had decided to withdraw her refugee protection claim the day after she had a fight with her mother, who had come to see her where she had been living since her mother had kicked her out of the house.

propositions.text: Applicant was panicking and upset about deteriorating relationship with mother.
propositions.quote: She stated that she was panicking and was upset by the state of her relationship with her mother, which was deteriorating a great deal.

propositions.text: Applicant called Immigration Canada to get passport back and prepared a note on January 19, 2011, to retract withdrawal but never sent it.
propositions.quote: She therefore called Immigration Canada to find out how to get her passport back. She stated that she prepared a note for Immigration Canada on January 19, 2011, indicating that she no longer wanted to withdraw her claim, a note that she allegedly never sent.

propositions.text: Applicant attached copy of unsent note to affidavit and explained she wanted lawyer's advice before sending it.
propositions.quote: She attached a copy of this note to her affidavit. She explained that she had not sent this note because she had been advised to hire a lawyer to make an application to reopen her file, and she had wanted to show this note to the lawyer before sending it.

propositions.text: Applicant now knows withdrawing claim was reckless.
propositions.quote: She also stated that she knows today that withdrawing her refugee protection claim was a reckless act.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes applicant's affidavit: withdrew claim after fight, panicked, tried to retract withdrawal but did not send note, and now regrets withdrawing claim.

propositions.text: RPD can reinstate claim only if natural justice was breached or if in interests of justice.
propositions.quote: The RPD's jurisdiction in terms of reinstating refugee protection claims is limited. In fact, once it has acknowledged the withdrawal, the RPD can only allow the reinstatement if there has been a failure to observe a principle of natural justice or if it is otherwise in the interests of justice to allow it.

propositions.text: Is there a failure to observe a principle of natural justice?
propositions.quote: Has there been a failure to observe a principle of natural justice?

paragraphs.summary: The court states RPD can reinstate only if natural justice breached or interests of justice, and poses the issue of natural justice breach.

propositions.text: No natural justice breach found; applicant voluntarily took steps to return to Colombia.
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the application to reinstate and the entire file, the panel cannot conclude, based on the evidence presented, that there has been a failure to observe a principle of natural justice, because the applicant voluntarily and without constraint took steps to return to her country, Colombia.

propositions.text: Applicant's father sent passport by UPS on December 20, 2010, before December 29 event.
propositions.quote: The evidence shows that her father sent his daughter's passport by UPS on December 20, 2010, so the applicant had told her father of her intention to return to Colombia by December 20, 2010, if not before.

propositions.text: Applicant booked flight to Colombia and took voluntary steps to return.
propositions.quote: She indicated that she had booked a flight to return to Colombia. She voluntarily took all of these steps in order to return to Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no natural justice breach; applicant voluntarily took steps to return to Colombia including passport and flight booking.

propositions.text: Applicant's failure to inform herself is not a natural justice breach attributable to the Board.
propositions.quote: Her failure to inform herself and the consequences that resulted from this do not represent a breach of natural justice that can be attributed to the Board.

propositions.text: Applicant alone responsible for consequences of withdrawing claim without necessary information.
propositions.quote: On the contrary, this situation is attributable entirely to her, and only she is responsible for it because it was her responsibility to get the necessary information before taking this significant step, which closed her file at the Board.

propositions.text: Applicant was an adult and could have sought counsel before withdrawing claim.
propositions.quote: The applicant was an adult when she made that decision. Nothing in the allegations presented to support her application indicates that she was unable to benefit from the advice of a counsel before filing her notice to withdraw her refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Is it in the interests of justice to reinstate the claim?
propositions.quote: Is it in the interests of justice to reinstate the refugee protection claim?

paragraphs.summary: The court finds applicant responsible for consequences, no natural justice breach by Board, and poses issue of interests of justice.

propositions.text: Rule 53 requires application under rule 44, which requires applications without delay.
propositions.quote: Rule 53 states that an application to reinstate a refugee protection claim must be made under rule 44, which states that all applications must be made "without delay".

propositions.text: Applicant withdrew claim December 30, 2010; application to reinstate received March 24, 2011, nearly three months later.
propositions.quote: The applicant withdrew her refugee protection claim on December 30, 2010. Her application to reinstate was received by the RPD on March 24, 2011, nearly three months later.

propositions.text: Applicant did not act without delay in applying to reinstate.
propositions.quote: The panel considers that the applicant did not act without delay.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes rule 53 requires no delay; applicant applied nearly three months later and did not act without delay.

propositions.text: Court considers Justice Snider's Federal Court judgment on reinstatement applications.
propositions.quote: The panel is taking into account the analysis done by Justice Snider of the Federal Court in a recent judgment,3 which deals with an application to reinstate and in which the judge states that subsection 53(3) requires a separate consideration of each ground where submissions on both grounds have been made.

propositions.text: Justice Snider refers to Justice Phelan's interpretation of 'in the interests of justice' as broad discretion requiring weighing all circumstances.
propositions.quote: In this decision, Justice Snider refers to the interpretation of the meaning of the words "in the interests of justice" in subsection 53(3) of the Rules, provided by Justice Michael Phelan in Ohanyan v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), as follows: The term "otherwise in the interests of justice" are broad words giving the Board a wide discretion to reinstate but which requires the Board to weigh all the circumstances of a case - not just from the vantage point of an applicant's interests.

propositions.text: Reinstatement is an exception and must be interpreted in that context.
propositions.quote: Reinstatement is an exception to the norm and must be interpreted and applied in that context.

paragraphs.summary: The court considers Federal Court analysis that reinstatement requires weighing all circumstances and is an exception to the norm.

propositions.text: Applicant's behavior in taking steps to return is inconsistent with fear of persecution claim.
propositions.quote: Although the applicant stated that she still fears being persecuted in Colombia, the panel considers that the applicant's behaviour in taking all the steps required to return to her country is not the behaviour of a person who claims to fear for her life if she returned to that country.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds applicant's actions inconsistent with claimed fear of persecution in Colombia.

propositions.text: Applicant did not explain why she did not take booked flight and did not send January 19 note to RPD.
propositions.quote: In addition, the applicant did not explain why she did not take the flight that she had booked for XXXX, 2011, to leave the country. The note that she wrote on January 19, 2011, was not sent to the RPD at that time.

propositions.text: Applicant said she wanted to consult lawyer before sending note but delayed consulting lawyer until March 2011 without explanation.
propositions.quote: She stated that she had wanted to consult a lawyer before sending it, but she did not consult a lawyer until March 2011, although she gave no explanation for this delay.

propositions.text: Note is a printed page and any date could have been written on it.
propositions.quote: This document is simply a printed page, and the panel notes that any date could have been written on this letter.

propositions.text: Applicant waited to get PIF copy but could have requested it from RPD office.
propositions.quote: She also stated that she was waiting to obtain a copy of her PIF before making her application to reinstate, and that after several requests, she had still not been able to obtain a copy of her PIF. However, had she made the request to the RPD office, she could have received a copy of her PIF on request.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes applicant did not explain flight non-use, delayed lawyer consultation, note date questionable, and could have requested PIF copy from RPD.

propositions.text: Evidence does not establish interests of justice to reinstate claim; application dismissed.
propositions.quote: For all of these reasons, the panel considers that the evidence provided does not establish that it would be in the interests of justice to reinstate the refugee protection claim. The present application to reinstate is therefore dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes evidence does not support reinstatement in interests of justice and dismisses the application.
